brief.premise: An independent insurance adjuster investigates the disappearance of a featured painting during a private gallery opening, reconstructing the evening from conflicting witness accounts, security logs, and sightline evidence.
brief.setting: Contemporary urban art gallery during a private exhibition opening — main hall, secure vault, director's office, lobby, and rooftop terrace
brief.investigator_character: Independent insurance adjuster retained to determine whether the loss was theft or a staged claim
brief.opening_situation: You arrive at the Meridian Contemporary after the opening-night alarm. Gallery director Vera Okonkwo reports a theft; curator Lina Morales and security chief James Holt give accounts that do not align.
initial_observable_facts: The featured painting Midnight Verdict is missing from its wall mount in the main hall.
Head of security James Holt claims the piece was secured in the vault until the 2100 alarm.
Curator Lina Morales says she noticed the empty wall during her podium remarks around 2055.
Collector Otto Weiss photographed activity near the painting shortly before the alarm.
brief.in_world_duration: one opening night (approximately three in-world hours)
brief.location_scale: single urban gallery with five primary locations
brief.content_boundaries: no graphic violence; no supernatural elements; insurance fraud and witness contradiction themes; no sexual content
required_themes: one perfect ending and several imperfect endings
brief.deadline_or_constraint: Carrier claim filing deadline at 2300; witnesses dispersing after midnight
brief.author_notes: Codename: The Gallery Verdict. Culprit NPC-VERA staged removal for insurance fraud after private sale. Emphasis on contradictory testimony, alibis, and sightlines — not burglary mechanics.

fixed_truth.method: Crate removal disguised as loan return during opening chaos, with coached contradictory witness accounts
